ambiguities.description: Cardinality of Instructor teaching offerings: The transcript states 'An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester.' However, it is unclear whether this allows an instructor to teach multiple offerings in different semesters, or whether there are other constraints on how many offerings an instructor can teach overall. The model assumes an instructor can teach multiple offerings without explicit bounds across all semesters.

source_references.excerpt: An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester

ambiguities.description: Course offering capacity vs enrollment: The transcript states that each offering has a maximum capacity, but does not explicitly state whether the system enforces this constraint (prevents enrollment beyond capacity) or merely tracks it. This is a business rule completeness question.

source_references.excerpt: Each offering has a maximum capacity -- a cap on how many students can enroll

ambiguities.description: CreditValue constraint precision: The transcript states 'usually between 1 and 6' for credit value, indicating a typical range but not an absolute hard constraint. It is unclear whether values outside this range (e.g., 0 or 7+) are permissible exceptions, or whether the 'usually' reflects only historical data and the actual constraint should be hardcoded. The model currently constrains to 1-6, but this may be an over-specification.

source_references.excerpt: The credit value is a whole number, usually between 1 and 6

ambiguities.description: Optionality of instructor participation: The model assumes every CourseOffering must have an instructor (mandatory constraint). However, the transcript does not explicitly state what happens if no instructor is assigned or if an offering runs without an assigned instructor. This should be clarified.

source_references.excerpt: Each offering is taught by exactly one instructor

ambiguities.description: Grade optionality and timing: The model assumes every Enrollment must have a Grade. However, the transcript states 'At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade', which could imply that grades are only assigned post-semester. It is unclear whether an enrollment record can exist in the early part of a semester without a grade assigned yet, or whether grades are always mandatory immediately upon enrollment.

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in

ambiguities.description: Many-to-many relationship between Student and CourseOffering: The model objectifies 'Student enrolls in CourseOffering' as an Enrollment entity. However, the transcript does not explicitly state whether a student can enroll in the same offering more than once (e.g., retaking the course). The current model allows only one enrollment per student-offering combination, but this should be verified.
